conclusions.conclusion: The close is partial: material source or close evidence remains unresolved. Revenue changed from 400 to 500.00, while bank collections changed from 450 to 250. Billings were 800; they are distinct from revenue and cash receipts. Gross billed receivables closed at 1520.00. Contract liability closed at 1300.00; it is not a receivable. The reviewed credit allowance closed at 80.00. Receivable FX contributed 10.00 to the AR movement, separately from billings and collections; it does not explain revenue growth. Unapplied cash of 50 remains a customer liability. The period was reopened and reclosed under reviewed authorization; a late-posted journal has supported economic cutoff and approval and is not automatically an accounting error. Older unpaid invoices require collection follow-up; the supplied evidence does not establish why each customer paid late. The claim that collections only look worse because revenue grew is rejected. The accounting owners support the recognition, credit allowance and FX amounts; these are accounting effects, not evidence of a commercial accounting error. Resolve the listed source/reconciliation contradictions before declaring the close clean. Preserve the original due dates and obtain the complete ageing export and reconciliation disposition. The allowance accounting check is supported by the reviewed workpaper.
